transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luca Ortiz, Priya Kapoor (Redwood) — Avery Cole, Dr. Mina Patel, Jon Rivera, Sam Norton, Elise Tan (StratoHealth)

Summary (auto): Onboarding blockers narrowed to VPC/bastion details and final security docs. SE to run benchmark with provided prompts.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): all right everyone uh thanks for joining on a Friday — I know some folks are wrapping up so we'll keep this tight. Quick roll call?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Avery): Avery here. Mina, Jon, Sam, Elise with me.
00:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): awesome thanks. Luca and Priya with me from Redwood. High level — short agenda: access readiness, security Qs, perf spike plan, and next steps.
00:25 Speaker 3 (Luca): hey team, I wanted to pick up where we left last week on the VPC peering and the bastion. Jon any update?
00:32 Speaker 4 (Jon): yeah so we've locked down the subnet ranges, mostly, um 10.20.0.0/16 for dev, 10.21.0.0/16 for staging. We'll need the Redwood egress IPs to open in our firewall. Also we prefer a bastion approach vs opening wide egress.
00:46 Speaker 3 (Luca): that's fine — we can provide a handful of static egress IPs for the peering plus an SSH bastion option. We'll send the list. Are you planning to NAT all outbound?
00:55 Speaker 4 (Jon): yes nat gateway in front, so static egress. We'll share the CIDR and NAT IPs.
01:02 Speaker 5 (Sam): quick security question — do you store any inference requests? Are there logs with PII? We need to know retention policy.
01:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): good question. For the pilot, Redwood hosted keeps minimal audit logs; we can toggle full request logging off. We also have an option for Dedicated or Private where logs can be customer-managed. We'll send the SOC2 extract showing data handling.
01:24 Speaker 5 (Sam): okay but KMS flow — if we use customer-managed keys, how does that work for a hosted model?
01:31 Speaker 3 (Luca): currently our hosted control plane can integrate with customer KMS via a dedicated key escrow flow — there's a handshake and rotation schedule. For full on-prem keys you'd move to Redwood Private. There's some nuance around tokenization and KV cache — the cache keys aren't stored in plain text.
01:47 Speaker 2 (Avery): hm, the KV cache bit worries our privacy team. Mina, did you want to chime in?
01:52 Speaker 6 (Mina): yeah just to say we need a short writeup about what elements are cached and for how long. Our bar is that patient data never persists beyond the request unless explicitly stored.
02:03 Speaker 1 (Maya): absolutely we'll provide that. Luca, can you prepare a 1-page cache behavior doc?
02:07 Speaker 3 (Luca): yep I can do that, quick note: by default KV cache keeps session state for up to 20 minutes with automatic eviction; we can turn that to session-only on your pilot.
02:18 Speaker 7 (Elise): curious about perf — our primary metric is 95th percentile latency at 512 tokens under p95 traffic. We need that number to be under 400ms ideally.
02:29 Speaker 3 (Luca): okay that's tight on hosted with default batching, we can tune batching windows and use a lower-latency variant. What's your target qps?
02:37 Speaker 2 (Avery): our initial spike is small — maybe 10 r/s, but bursty. We care more about tail latency than sustained throughput.
02:45 Speaker 3 (Luca): got it. For bursts we'll recommend lower batch sizes and a smaller batching timeout, and if needed a dedicated pool to guarantee tail SLOs. That said dedicated raises cost.
02:57 Speaker 5 (Sam): cost is a factor — your pricing for dedicated vs hosted? We need a ballpark to compare to Vertex and Anthropic.
03:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll send a tailored estimate based on the qps and model choice. For pilot we usually recommend hosted but with allocation of burst headroom; if tail latency is non-negotiable, Dedicated is the right lane. We'll include a delta table in the follow-up.
03:19 Speaker 6 (Mina): on model variants — we want to test a fp16 baseline and a quantized 4-bit to see if quality degrades. Any guidance?
03:27 Speaker 3 (Luca): quantized will reduce token cost and usually helps latency slightly, but there can be hallucination regressions. We can run A/B with your eval prompts to measure quality delta. For the pilot we'll try both.
03:40 Speaker 7 (Elise): what's the timeline to get the perf numbers?
03:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): Luca — how long to run the benchmark once we have the prompt set and network info?
03:49 Speaker 3 (Luca): two business days for 3 runs, maybe 24–48 hours if we prioritize. I'll need the prompt set and the CIDR/NAT IPs to mirror the network.
03:58 Speaker 4 (Jon): we'll provide the prompt set and the NAT IPs by Tues (that's 3/31).
04:03 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect. We'll target results by Friday.
04:06 Speaker 5 (Sam): on SSO — we use SAML via Okta, need to map roles into RBAC. Any docs?
04:13 Speaker 3 (Luca): yes, SAML mapping guide and sample metadata will be in the packet Maya shares. You can map groups to roles; we support SCIM for user sync if you prefer.
04:23 Speaker 6 (Mina): audit logs — can we route them to our Splunk?
04:27 Speaker 3 (Luca): for hosted we can forward logs to your endpoint via an encrypted syslog; for Private we integrate directly. We'll document options.
04:36 Speaker 2 (Avery): also need to validate data residency — some PII needs to remain in US-east only. Do you have region pinning?
04:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes region pinning available on Dedicated and for Hosted most models are in us-east and we can pin customers to specific clusters; we'll confirm which models are in which regions.
04:55 Speaker 7 (Elise): any gotchas with VPC peering and egress for low latency? We don't want an extra hop.
05:00 Speaker 3 (Luca): if you peer directly with our dedicated egress in the same region, hops are minimal. Using NAT and a bastion adds small overhead but usually sub-10ms. We'll include network topology diagrams.
05:12 Speaker 5 (Sam): call out: we may need PCI-like assurances later, so can you share any compliance posture docs?
05:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes SOC2+ISO extract will be in the pack. For PCI we can discuss scope later — typically Private is the route.
05:28 Speaker 3 (Luca): quick demo note — when we run perf tests we'll surface per-token breakdowns and KV cache hit rates in the debug logs; that should help with SLO tuning.
05:37 Speaker 6 (Mina): perfect. Also can you stash the model versions? We want deterministic pins for evaluation.
05:41 Speaker 3 (Luca): absolutely — we'll pin model hashes and include a rollout plan.
05:47 Speaker 2 (Avery): any blockers from Redwood's side?
05:51 Speaker 1 (Maya): none besides waiting for your NAT IPs and prompt set. Also I'll need Sam to confirm the minimal logging requirement for the pilot.
06:00 Speaker 5 (Sam): I can confirm: no request bodies in logs, only metadata for now.
06:05 Speaker 3 (Luca): noted — we'll disable request-body logging and provide a config snippet.
06:10 Speaker 7 (Elise): timeline recap?
06:13 Speaker 1 (Maya): Jon sends CIDR/NAT by Tues 3/31. Mina shares prompt set and p95 target by 3/30. Luca runs perf and uploads CSV by 4/02. Maya shares security pack and SAML guide by 3/30. Follow-up deep-dive on quantization week of 4/6.
06:29 Speaker 2 (Avery): sounds good. Any other questions?
06:33 Speaker 6 (Mina): one last ask — can you annotate which logs might include PII so our DPO can review?
06:39 Speaker 3 (Luca): yes I'll add an explicit column in the log export doc.
06:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): great. I'll send calendar invite for the quantization deep-dive. Thanks everyone, we'll close on these action items.
06:50 Speaker 4 (Jon): thanks all.
06:52 Speaker 5 (Sam): thanks.
06:54 Speaker 1 (Maya): bye.

Note: transcription contains occasional speaker attribution errors and filler words; some acronyms may be mis-typed (e.g., KVcache vs KV cache).
